title: Building State of the Art Open Weights Tool Use: The Command R Family: Sandra Kublik

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk centers on how Command R/R+ were post-trained for RAG and tool use, with a section explicitly dedicated to post-training solutions for RAG challenges. The models are general-purpose LLMs optimized for RAG (search_and_knowledge) with an open-sourced developer UI toolkit (developer_platforms). The talk covers post-training optimization and production deployment of the Command R family to the community. The talk covers technical RAG and tool use concepts at a level accessible to practicing developers. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair. Claims are stated in the transcript with supporting metrics but without independent verification.

summary: Sandra Kublik of Cohere presents the Command R and R+ open-weight model family, emphasizing their strengths in structured advanced RAG, sequential reasoning, and tool use. Command R, released March 11, was optimized for retrieval-augmented generation and designed to be scalable and GPU-friendly. Command R+ followed, optimized for advanced RAG and tool use, and quickly topped the LMSYS Arena. Community response was strong: the model trended on OpenRouter within two weeks, saw 150,000 Hugging Face downloads, and was adopted by Hugging Face as the base for HuggingChat. Nearly half a million developers and researchers now use the R family. Notable community projects include a coding assistant by Daniel S, a generative search demo by Complexity, and two Discord bots. Kublik outlines key RAG challenges that Cohere addressed through post-training: prompt sensitivity, the model's bias toward the beginning of documents, and the tension between pre-trained knowledge and externally retrieved context. The models were optimized to decide when external information is needed and to operate retrieval systems smoothly. Fine-grained citations are a major focus, tested on the Kilt dataset with best-in-class performance. On April 24, Cohere open-sourced a UI toolkit repo with plug-and-play Next.js components, a SQL conversation-history database, customizable model access, and a retrieval component built on LChain. Tool use is divided into single-step (independent actions) and multi-step (sequential, building actions). A multi-step API released the prior week lets the model create a plan, call tools, reflect on results, and adapt. Command R+ is competitive with Claude Opus and GPT-4 Turbo at three-to-five-times lower cost, with near-parity on complex reasoning benchmarks.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Model Family Overview
sections.summary: Kublik introduces the Command R family as state-of-the-art open-weight models excelling at structured advanced RAG and sequential reasoning, competitive with GPT-4 Turbo and Claude Opus while being smaller and locally runnable.

sections.title: Release Timeline and Community Response
sections.summary: Command R was released March 11 for RAG; Command R+ followed for tool use and advanced RAG, topping LMSYS Arena within days. The community responded with 150,000 Hugging Face downloads, OpenRouter trending status, and adoption as HuggingChat's base model. Notable projects include a coding assistant, generative search demo, and two Discord bots.

sections.title: RAG Challenges and Post-Training Solutions
sections.summary: Kublik details three core RAG challenges—prompt sensitivity, document-position bias, and knowledge steering between pre-trained and retrieved information. Post-training optimized the model to decide when external information is needed, operate retrieval systems, and use grounded context, addressing these out of the box.

sections.title: Citations, Performance, and Open-Sourced UI
sections.summary: Fine-grained citations are a major focus, validated on the Kilt dataset with best-in-class performance and low hallucination. On April 24, Cohere open-sourced a UI toolkit repo with plug-and-play Next.js components, SQL conversation history, customizable model access across providers, and an LChain-based retrieval component with document upload and web search.

sections.title: Tool Use Optimization and Multi-Step API
sections.summary: Tool use is divided into single-step (independent actions) and multi-step (sequential reasoning with reflection and error correction). A multi-step API was released the prior week: the model creates a plan, calls tools, reflects on results, and adapts. A large multi-step preamble prompt is available on Hugging Face. Command R+ is competitive with GPT-4 Turbo and Claude Opus at 3-5x lower cost.

demonstrations: Generative search demo by Complexity (planned live demo)
Two Discord server bots: one playful for demonstrating model capabilities, one helpful grounded in Cohere docs and API information
HuggingChat using Command R+ as base model with doc parser, image editor, and calculator
limitations: Building RAG is described as excruciatingly hard with numerous challenges
Models are highly prompt sensitive in RAG contexts
Models have a natural bias toward focusing on the beginning of documents
Creating UX/UI for RAG and tool use is described as super painful
Steering between pre-trained knowledge and external prompt information is an ongoing battle
